messages.subject: Estimate a censored poisson model
parts:
Hello,

I have seen that this topic has been discussed elsewhere, but I couldn't seem to understand the discourse fully (hence why I'm asking this question).

I have data like: 0 1 0 2 3 4 4 4 4 -- where the data is censored at 4 (so each time a 4 appears it means the data is >= 4). I would like to use a Poisson distribution to model this data, allowing for the fact that I know that 4 is the censoring point.

How can I do this? 

(I have seen references to the incomplete gamma (which I don't think Stan has), but also the potential to sum over all feasible (so non-infinite) values of the pmf for 4 and greater.)

Best,

Ben

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Estimate a censored poisson model
parts:
This is discussed in the “Integrating Out Censored Values” section of the manual.
For the Poisson distribution with unaggregated censored values this would look
something like

for (n n 1:N)
  if (k[n] < 3)
    target += poisson_lpmf(k[n] | lambda);
  else
    target += poisson_lccdf(3 | lambda);

Note the “3” in the complimentary cumulative distribution function as you want
to integrating the tail probability _including_ 4 for the censored observations.
